messages:
sara: Quick question — I'm prepping a TF change to add a GPU node pool for the new inference cluster. Wanted a quick sanity check on instance choices + capacity reservation strategy. TL;DR: can we use mixed spot + reserved fallback?

mike: yes, mixed is fine. We usually prefer stable instance families (g5/p4) and reserve a small on-demand capacity for critical pods. how much baseline qps are you planning for?

sara: baseline ~200 concurrent tokens/sec across 3 replicas, bursty up to ~800 for short windows. thinking g5.12xlarge for most workloads, p4d for high-memory models. question: how do people wire the capacity reservation in our TF module?

jon: @sara we added a small capacity_reservation block in the aws_node_group module last year. pattern: create a dedicated on-demand sub-group with min_size = reserved_count, taint it so only critical pods get scheduled. spot group is default for scale-out.

lina: fwiw for k8s: use node taints + pod tolerations + nodeSelector labels to enforce critical placement. also set kubelet --eviction to be strict for spot nodes.

sara: sharing the snippet I'm planning to add to infra/modules/gpu_node_pool/main.tf: ```hcl
module "gpu_node_pool" {
  source = "../modules/aws_node_group"
  instance_types = ["g5.12xlarge", "g5.8xlarge"]
  spot = true
  fallback_on_demand = true
  reserved_capacity = 2
  labels = { role = "gpu", tier = "inference" }
}
``` can someone call out obvious pitfalls?

mike: two quick notes: 1) add instance_types that are compatible for pod topology spread (avoid mixing radically different GPUs if scheduler matters). 2) reserved_capacity should map to a second on-demand node_group resource so TF doesn't try to flip a spot ASG into reserved.

jon: also add lifecycle rule to prevent accidental drift recreates for the on-demand group. and ensure autoscaling group launch template includes the same AMI and drivers.

lina: secrets wiring: if nodes need to fetch model keys from our KMS-proxy, add iam_role with kms:Decrypt and attach the kube secret via projected service account token + iam role for service accounts. do NOT put KMS keys in user_data.

sara: good call. for the kube manifests I'm planning: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Node
metadata:
  labels:
    role: gpu
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: nvidia-drivers
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - key: "gpu"
        operator: "Exists"
      containers:
      - name: installer
        image: "redwood/nvidia-driver-installer:stable"
``` is that too heavy-handed?

mike: don't create Node objects directly. use nodeSelector labels via the bootstrap/user_data. DaemonSet is fine for drivers but prefer a gentle rollout and check image size.

deploy-bot: autoscaler event: scaled up gpu-spot-asg from 0 to 3 instances (reason: cpu/pods)

jon: code-review ping @mike @lina — opened PR: infra#312 (adds gpu_node_pool module & docs). Highlights: separate on-demand reserved ASG, spot ASG with mixed instances, taints for critical placement, SA + IRSA for KMS access.

mike: reviewing now, will comment on the AMI boot order and launch template security groups. please add a migration note for existing clusters.

lina: I can add the k8s toleration examples and a small test plan for node failover (simulate spot termination).

sara: thanks all. I'll wait for PR notes and then roll the TF change in canary env first. if anyone wants to test the driver DaemonSet in staging ping me and I'll coordinate. :thumbsup:
